source.title: Lorentz Entailment Cone for Semantic Segmentation
source.authors: Zahid Hasan; Masud Ahmed; Nirmalya Roy

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; title differs slightly from the catalog title, but the paper identity is corroborated by its reference [25].
record.tranche_reason: The study measures loss-landscape flatness for Lorentz and Euclidean segmentation models and argues that flatter minima align with improved generalization. This is a different measure bearing on V7, though it does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure or directly quantify train–test gaps.
record.gate_note: The paper reports segmentation performance and geometric/gradient results. Only the loss-landscape flatness comparison directly bears on a mapped version. Training performance metrics do not compare training and test error gaps; cited findings and qualitative segmentation or uncertainty claims do not establish the mapped memorization/generalization versions.
record.test_reason: Section 5.4 reports qualitative loss-surface flatness and invokes a general flatness–generalization link. It does not measure generalization gaps or test their association with sharpness. Segmentation performance and the other experiments do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 5.4: the authors report flatter Lorentz minima, interpret them through an established flatness–generalization link, and leave the explanation for future work. Their broader conclusion also emphasizes hierarchical consistency, zero-shot segmentation, uncertainty estimation, and low-dimensional representational efficiency. They do not establish V7's sharpness–gap relationship.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a Lorentz hyperbolic segmentation framework with text-guided prototype and entailment losses; its loss-surface comparison is qualitative and does not reproduce the magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or train–test gap analysis described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The qualitative comparison is shown for DeepLabV3 on Cityscapes and SegFormer on COCO-Stuff; no cross-condition sensitivity analysis of the sharpness–gap relationship is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Filter-normalized, two-direction loss-surface visualizations show smoother Lorentz surfaces than Euclidean counterparts for DeepLabV3 on Cityscapes and SegFormer on COCO-Stuff.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested Lorentz segmentation models converge to qualitatively flatter minima than their Euclidean counterparts.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The loss-surface evidence is qualitative and limited to visualizations; no numeric sharpness measure or train–test gap is reported, and the text says a detailed analysis of the loss gradients is beyond scope.
record.rows_left_out: Segmentation mIoU, hyperbolicity estimates, zero-shot results, and gradient visualizations do not measure the mapped versions' claims about memorization/generalization gaps or magnitude-aware sharpness. Loss-landscape result retained as R1.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under controlled tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
The association between magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text identifies itself as arXiv:2604.16836 and explicitly extends the WACV paper cited as reference [25]. This indicates a source-identity mismatch with the requested WACV DOI; citing that earlier paper does not corroborate that they are the same study. This assessment applies to the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label performance.
Width sweeps past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch comparisons under epoch budgets.

The study qualitatively compares Lorentz and Euclidean loss landscapes, but does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, rank gaps across networks with similarly low training loss, compare norm- or margin-based measures, or report train–test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Lorentz model (DeepLabV3 cityscape; SegFormer COCO-Stuff)
rows.operation_detail: Visualizes loss surfaces after perturbing weights along two random directions following filter normalization; compares Lorentz and Euclidean models.
rows.value: Lorentz model consistently achieves smoother loss than Euclidean.
rows.note: Qualitative loss-landscape comparison only; it does not measure V7's weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or train–test gap.
rows.check: The reported smoother Lorentz loss surfaces are supported by Section 5.4 and Figure 16, but cannot establish V7's sharpness–gap relationship. Filter-normalized random-direction visualizations do not report perturbation tolerance before training error rises, matched training losses, or train–test gaps. Missing measurements are not evidence of a partial effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
